Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

readboj 0.2.0

  • Adds calendar-aware maintain_boj_outlook(), official Outlook/holiday discovery, local maintenance status and installed --maintenance mode. Persists separate Bank’s View/full-text stages, UTC next-due times, catch-up/retry state and cheap metadata probes. Calendar outages preserve prior evidence without blocking independently due data updates; ordinary reads remain saved-only.
  • Makes ordinary list_boj_outlook_releases() and read_boj_outlook() calls read memoized saved numeric data with no network, raw PDF reads or extractor. Bundles all 74 verified editions (4,142 rows, five NA markers). General source discovery/parsing remains explicit through the corresponding _raw() functions.
  • Adds update_boj_outlook(), local freshness/status and a full bundle builder. Checks every linked source for new editions, changed links and historical revisions; validates complete candidates before atomic publication. Readers consume refreshed user data while the package baseline stays read-only. Adds writer exclusion, last-good fallback, daily throttling, bounded raw staging cleanup and installed/repository daily scheduling entrypoints.
  • Rejects revised tables that lose existing scalar identities/targets by default; reviewed coverage-loss opt-in records removed identities and retains old rows. Makes failed-throttled daily runs exit nonzero, with quiet repeated watch failures and explicit recovery reporting.
  • Derives measure definitions, fiscal horizons, statistics, comparator vintages, actuals and conditional point estimates from source tables/notes. Preserves WPI/CGPI, tax/education-adjusted CPI, shared cells, separate all-member ranges and the pandemic member-interval construction without inventing medians.
  • Retains bounded raw caching, offline replay, source pins and optional Poppler extraction under one deadline. Adds HTML XPath/PDF bounding boxes, source publication metadata and per-edition receipts. No runtime R dependency is added.
  • Verifies all 74 archive editions and retains the original 167-cell regression, held-out full-table checks and format-transition/semantic/failure tests.

readboj 0.1.1

  • Fixes bounded Shift-JIS/CP932 response validation so a byte limit that lands inside a multibyte character is trimmed to the preceding complete line.
  • Adds deterministic split-character coverage and a live IR02 bilingual metadata canary.
  • Expands the user-facing documentation, reference articles, vignettes, package metadata, pkgdown configuration, and contributor/support guidance for a deterministic pre-CRAN workflow.
  • Adds a prominent retrieve-select-chart workflow for the official FM08/FXERM07 series, with a provenance-recorded rendered figure and an offline documentation path.
  • Standardizes the package author, maintainer, citation, and copyright-holder display to Chartwell Macro.
  • Adds CRAN-readiness checks and release documentation. These documentation and release-engineering changes do not alter exported signatures, defaults, output schemas/classes/attributes, cache behavior, endpoints, or provider behavior; the CP932 response-boundary fix above is the only runtime correction recorded for 0.1.1.

readboj 0.1.0

  • Adds bounded, paginated retrieval from all three official Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API operations.
  • Adds exact raw-response snapshots, SHA-256 provenance, cache/offline replay, a semantic API hash that excludes only the volatile response DATE, and automatic total cache bounds.
  • Adds stable English/Japanese metadata fields and streamed, result-bounded search suitable for the large Tankan catalogue.
  • Adds portable atomic catalogue snapshots with complete per-database counts, source URL/hash pins and fully offline bounded search.
  • Adds official bulk-file and dated Tankan release-asset discovery/download.
  • Adds bounded text-preserving XLS/XLSX parsing for official catalogues and Tankan workbooks.
  • Supports both official JSON and English/Japanese CSV observation responses, one caller-owned absolute deadline, HTTPS/host/redirect allowlists, success-only cache entries and typed transport/identity/corruption failures.
  • Ships synthetic structural fixtures and opt-in representative live checks.
